sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: RuView is a beta platform that uses WiFi signals as a sensor. Low-cost ESP32 boards read how people disturb radio waves, and models turn that into presence detection, breathing and heart-rate estimates and activity signals, without cameras.
sixtySeconds.problem: Cameras and wearables are intrusive for monitoring rooms. RuView explores camera-free sensing from WiFi Channel State Information (CSI), with smart-home integrations, though the README is clear that several capabilities are still experimental.
whoFor: Makers and researchers experimenting with WiFi sensing
AI agent users who want to operate sensors through MCP
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want to experiment with WiFi sensing on cheap hardware and are comfortable with beta software. Read the README's labels: some results are strong, some are explicitly weak, and pose accuracy is still limited.
requirements: ESP32-S3 boards (ESP32-C3 and original ESP32 are not supported)
Two or more nodes recommended for better spatial resolution
Optional: Home Assistant or another smart-home hub

overview: RuView captures Channel State Information from ESP32 sensors and runs signal processing and small models to estimate presence, occupancy, breathing rate, heart rate and activity. A pretrained model is published on Hugging Face. Edge modules can run directly on the ESP32 with no internet.

It integrates with Home Assistant over MQTT and can act as a Matter bridge for Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings. The @ruvnet/ruview package provides a command-line operator with device access, firmware flashing, an MCP server for AI agents and a Claude Code mod.

The project labels its own results. It calls itself beta, says single-node setups have limited spatial resolution, and reports camera-free pose accuracy as limited (around 2.5% PCK@20 with proxy labels). A unified RF world model is described as synthetic until real-data validation.

troubleshooting.problem: Using an ESP32-C3 or original ESP32
troubleshooting.solution: Not supported; they are single-core and can't handle CSI processing. Use ESP32-S3.
Single-node setups have limited resolution. Use two or more nodes.
Camera-free pose accuracy is still limited, as the README states.
